rule.description: A named struct type carries multiple unrelated responsibilities. Its declared production (non-test) method set decomposes into disjoint field-sharing clusters: groups of methods whose only connection is that they read or write some of the same receiver instance fields, with no instance state shared between groups. The rule fires when (a) the type is a classical god class (>= 10 methods spread across >= 2 package files forming >= 3 disjoint clusters) or (b) a concentrated god class (>= 6 methods forming >= 4 disjoint clusters regardless of file placement). Call edges are deliberately excluded: god classes routinely route work through their own methods, so call edges erase the very signal that distinguishes separate responsibilities.

checks.description: Detect named struct types whose declared method set splits into disjoint instance-field clusters, each cluster being a separate responsibility exercised through one type.
checks.detected_relation: receiver-bound method set -> disjoint instance-field clusters on one named struct type
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A type whose method groups share no instance state with each other is simultaneously the format registry, the disk-gathering configurator, the virtual-file-system mounter, the archive-creation coordinator, and the extraction/policy engine; every group changes for different reasons and has its own lifecycle, yet they are all reached through one declaration and one 'default' instance.

matches.evidence: The format-registry responsibility is absorbed into the all-purpose type: RegisterFormat, Identify, identifyOne, readAtMost, SupportedFormats, and ByExtension all operate on the receiver's private registry map, in the same type that also performs disk walking, archive creation, and extraction. Diagnostic: cluster accessing receiver field(s) [formats] through methods [ByExtension, Identify, RegisterFormat, SupportedFormats].

The on-disk file-gathering responsibility walks the filesystem from inside the same type, driven by the type's own symlink/attribute policy fields (FilesFromDisk with nameOnDiskToNameInArchive mapping). Diagnostic: cluster accessing receiver field(s) [ClearAttributes, FollowSymlinks] through methods [FilesFromDisk].

The virtual-file-system presentation responsibility is fused into the same type: FileSystem mounts archives/streams as io/fs file systems and scopes them with the type's Prefix field, with stream sizing done by the type's own streamSizeBySeeking method. Diagnostic: cluster accessing receiver field(s) [Prefix] through methods [FileSystem].

The archive-creation responsibility lives on the same type: ArchiveFolder picks the output format from the destination name, gathers inputs, and applies the type's ImplicitTopLevelFolder layout policy when writing the archive. Diagnostic: cluster accessing receiver field(s) [ImplicitTopLevelFolder] through methods [ArchiveFolder].

The extraction orchestration responsibility (detect the archive format from the stream, iterate entries, tolerate per-entry failures) is a method of the same all-purpose type, applying the type's ContinueOnError error policy. Diagnostic: cluster accessing receiver field(s) [ContinueOnError] through methods [ExtractToFolder].

The extraction file-writing responsibility (create dirs, recreate links, copy bodies) is also a method of the same type, governed by the type's OverwriteExisting on-disk collision policy and its destinationPath confinement helper. Diagnostic: cluster accessing receiver field(s) [OverwriteExisting] through methods [writeFileToDisk].

excluded.location: format implementation structs such as Zip (zip.go), Tar (tar.go), Rar (rar.go), and the compression formats (gz.go, bz2.go, ...)
excluded.reason: their method sets are confined to one file, hold at most two disjoint state clusters, and stay under the size thresholds; concentrating a single format's options in its implementation struct is cohesive, not a god class

excluded.location: presentation structs such as ArchiveFS and FileFS (fs.go)
excluded.reason: their methods operate one io/fs concern with at most two disjoint state clusters; they are medium-sized, single-responsibility adapter types

excluded.location: package-level convenience functions (Identify, RegisterFormat, FileSystem, FilesFromDisk, readAtMost, streamSizeBySeeking)
excluded.reason: the rule measures receiver-bound method sets on named struct types; package functions carry no receiver state to cluster

excluded.location: method sets declared only in _test.go files
excluded.reason: test doubles and assertion helpers are not production responsibilities; the analyzer only counts production (non-test) files
